lines.text: Oswin had faced frost-wolves, a frost-wyrm and my brother's fire without a flicker. In front of that old woman, he went white.
Madam. I... yes. I was there. At Ashby.
Ashby. The village that couldn't pay its taxes. The one he had refused to burn, with the villagers still inside.
They burned it anyway, the day after I said no. I've known that every day for two years. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.
Sit down, Sir Oswin. You're blocking my light.
I'm Edda. I was the reeve's wife in Ashby. We heard you that day. You stood in the road in front of the lord's horse, and you shouted at him for an hour.
An hour, Sir Oswin. In that hour, I took thirty-one people out through the back fields. Children, mostly. By the time his men came with the torches, we were in the woods.
Thirty-one of us are alive because of you. We live here now. We never knew your name, until today.
One by one, they came out of the crooked houses. A blacksmith with burn scars on his arms. Two young women with babies. A boy of about twelve. Thirty-one people who should have been ashes.
Oswin got down on his knees in the mud and cried like a child. I had never seen a knight cry. Nobody laughed.
I asked Edda the name of the lord who gave the order. She spat in the mud before she said it.
Lord Roderick Stane. He's here, in Aldcrown. He's riding in the King's Tourney.
We saw him the next day, riding to the lists. Red and gold armour, polished like a mirror. Five rings on five fingers, every one of them milky glass.
My lord. Seven rings around an eye. On every one of them.
His horse splashed mud over three Ashby children. He didn't look down.
Then he saw Oswin.
Hale. I heard you'd drunk yourself to death in a ditch somewhere in the north. What a pity. You cost me a village, you know. The King's taxes came out of it anyway. One way or another.
Frost crept over Oswin's knuckles. Over the hilt of his sword. Up his sleeves. I put my hand on his arm. It was colder than mine.
Not here. Not like this.
Run along, Hale. The Tourney is for lords.
Oswin didn't drink that night. He sat by the window and sharpened his sword until dawn.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty-two, coming soon.
